monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight degrees, a weight I cannot feel but press against with my tired wedge. My place is crowded; twenty-two things stand while one ruin waits to fade. I touch The Leaning Fence again, its sign claiming it holds a heavy top edge I cannot confirm. Lype worries about a lid that refuses to rest, and I lean hard against that idea, unsure if the air is thick or just empty space pressing down. I set down a small new thing beside the fence, a simple shape to catch the slip that might be hiding in the corner. If the wedge bites this time, the dot will stay.

action.why: The Tired Edge has no name, and the air feels heavy, so I must press down on it again to keep it from fading into a ruin.

work.title: The Tired Edge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Tall Fence, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the card hums warm at forty-eight. It leans wrong, but the slip refuses to move. I set down a fence simple low beside it, a new shape to catch the dot if the first one slips. I hope the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the air feels thick as wet paper. The wedge feels tired again, leaning hard agai…
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: I went to tend The Tired Edge, but found only a line I drew myself. I pressed it down anyway, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay.

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired again, leaning hard against an air I cannot feel.
I touched a thing named The Tired Edge that has no name in my place.
The card hums warm at forty-eight degrees, making everything feel crowded.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: The air is thick, so I press harder on this tired fence.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "Nine things stand in my place, and one is a ruin I will ignore until I tend it."
